glass_felix: My previous note suggesting cupboard_k1 as the primary evening spot was incorrect for day 7. The glass spent the entire day (08:00–22:00) at kitchen_table_k1, only moving to cupboard_k1 at the very end (22:59). Do not assume it is in the cupboard during the day or early evening; check kitchen_table_k1 first for any query before 23:00. Only default to cupboard_k1 for late-night queries after 23:00.

mug_felix: My previous note about cycling between desk_b1 and coffee_table_l1 was wrong for day 7. At 08:27, it was at kitchen_table_k1, not counter_k1. There is no evidence of it being in the bedroom or living room today. Check kitchen_table_k1 as the primary location for morning queries. Avoid assuming it is in the bedroom desk or living room coffee table without specific recent evidence.

tablet_felix: I consistently mislocated this item. At 08:27, it was at kitchen_table_k1 (I said bed_b1). At 20:54, it was at bed_b1 (I said desk_b1). It appears to follow a standard day-to-night migration: kitchen table in the morning, bedroom bed in the evening. Check kitchen_table_k1 for morning/afternoon queries and bed_b1 for evening queries. Do not guess desk_b1.

glasses_felix: My previous note about bathroom_shelf_ba1 in the morning was correct for 08:07. However, my assumption that it moves to coffee_table_l1 in the evening was wrong. At 21:31, it was at bed_b1. Check bathroom_shelf_ba1 for early morning queries and bed_b1 for late evening queries. Do not default to coffee_table_l1.

General Note: My assumption that Felix’s items follow erratic or static patterns is flawed. The tablet follows a predictable kitchen-to-bedroom path. The glass stays in the kitchen until very late. The glasses move from bathroom to bedroom. Always prioritize the most recent confirmed location over assumed patterns, but recognize that some items (tablet) have predictable daily cycles while others (glass) have delayed transitions.
